2. Opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 163 of 2003 in the 2nd Court of the Assistant Judge, Dhaka, against defendant No. 7 who is the present petitioner and others claiming a decree for restraining defendant No. 2 to release the amount of back to back L/C No. 18780360047 to defendant Nos.3 and 4 or any other defendants on their behalf by a decree of permanent Injunction and also restraining defendant Nos. 3 and 4 from receiving any payment in respect of back to back L/C No.  18780360047 dated 23-2-2003 from defendant Nos. 2 along with costs. 

 9. I have heard the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner and perused the revisional application along with other materials on record. It appears that the plaintiff filed a suit with a prayer for restraining defendant No. 2 to release the account of the back to back L/C to defendant Nos. 3 and 4 by way of a decree of permanent injunction and also restraining defendant Nos.3 and 4 from receiving any payment in respect of the said back to back L/C dated 23-2-2003 from defend-ant No. 2 as defendant No. 3 shipped the goods which were of inferior quality then what was stated in the proforma invoice.
